summary: Blue Lagoon is a spatial puzzle where you race to claim resource-rich hexes by carefully extending chains of settlers and villages, with the mid-game reset forcing you to have planted village 'seeds' in the right spots for phase two. It plays fast and tense, with much of the game coming down to reading the shrinking board and picking exactly the right placement each turn rather than any real negotiation.
praised: Elegant, easy-to-teach rules producing a surprisingly tight strategic puzzle
Strong tension from the two-phase structure (villages placed in phase one become the only expansion points in phase two)
Quick playtime with high replayability due to variable island setups
criticised: Can feel like solitaire/parallel optimization with limited direct player interaction beyond spatial blocking
Snowballing/positional advantage for whoever secures key spots early, especially with experienced players
Some analysis paralysis in the placement decisions despite simple rules
Scoring math (set collection tiers) can feel a bit fiddly for new players

interaction.kind: blocking and area denial via tile placement

scoring.why: Points come from multiple resource sets, giant sea creatures, and largest connected network, so the winner is whoever balances several scoring channels rather than maxing one
